hypothesis: The graph-cut partitioner's area-balance test uses a single global tolerance `area_balance_error` applied to `total_area`; tightening it from 10% to 5% forces the initial greedy and swap-based partitions to keep the two dies closer to equal area, reducing extreme die imbalance that causes long cross-tier detours and legalization displacement — a cheap, attributable probe of P-P4.
expected_effect: WNS roughly unchanged or slightly better; TNS modestly better (fewer long cross-tier nets needing repair); overflow unchanged (<=300); runtime ~same.
analysis: The hypothesis did not hold: tightening area balance from 10% to 5% gave total −0.049 (robust −0.020), with all three cases slightly negative. Ariane133-ng45 improved WNS (+6.8%) but lost TNS (−6.6%); bp-ng45 and bp_fe-ng45 show mixed WNS/TNS with no clear imbalance-driven gain, suggesting the tighter tolerance added partitioning/legalization cost without reducing cross-tier detours. Next step: sweep tolerance (e.g., 10/7.5/5%) and log per-die area skew versus cross-tier wirelength and displacement to test the proposed mechanism directly rather than inferring it from WNS/TNS.
